reason: I want to build the route from blood vessels toward tissues, so starting with an artery seems useful.
expectation: I expect a lined artery that can carry blood under pressure.

alternatives.reason: Capillaries are central to exchange, but I chose to start with the route leading toward them.

effect: The lined artery is built; I can now work on the smaller vessels that connect it to tissues.
reaction: The stretching and recoiling picture makes the artery's elastic wall feel purposeful.
reason: Capillaries are the next part of the route and bring blood close to tissues for exchange.
expectation: I expect a lined network of small capillaries, though I am unsure how it will connect to the artery.

alternatives.reason: A lined vein will also be needed for the return route, but I want to build the exchange vessels first.

effect: The capillary bed provides the thin-walled exchange network, so I can connect it to the artery.
reaction: The explanation makes the thin walls' purpose clear.
reason: Connecting the artery to the capillaries starts joining the route toward tissues.
expectation: I expect an arterial route connected to the capillary bed.

alternatives.reason: The vein will be needed for the return route, but I want to connect the vessels already built first.

effect: The artery now feeds a capillary network spread across the tissue; the return route still needs to be built.
reaction: The parallel branches make it clear how blood reaches a broad area.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and a lined vein should provide part of the return route.
expectation: I expect a lined venous vessel, possibly still needing valves before it joins the route.

effect: The lined veins are ready for valve folds before joining the return route.
reaction: The wide, thin-walled vein contrasts clearly with the artery.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and valves should help keep blood moving in one direction.
expectation: I expect veins fitted with valves that help prevent blood from flowing backward.

effect: The valves and surrounding muscle together explain how blood can move toward the heart; the return route is ready to connect.
reaction: The muscle compression and valve picture makes the return mechanism clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the route through tissues.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries through capillaries to veins.

effect: The completed network connects the artery, capillary bed and veins into a route through tissues, with arteries carrying blood away from the heart and veins returning it.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the separate vessels form a complete route.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding valves to the veins was most worthwhile: the description showed how contracting muscle and valves work together to move blood toward the heart.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled veins felt least engaging on its own; the result mostly named and pictured the parts already implied by the combination.

surprise.text: The role of contracting limb muscles in helping venous return added something I had not expected from the valve combination alone.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The lining and wall combinations had clear purposes, although several later steps were the only offered choices.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it connected this vessel network to the heart and showed blood moving through the larger circulation. The exchange and return mechanisms made me curious about that next connection.
